title: Think Before You Buy
source_body:
These days, clothes are cheaper than ever. Many stores sell T-shirts for the price of a sandwich, and new styles appear almost every week. This trend is called fast fashion. It may seem convenient, but I believe we should buy fewer clothes and wear them longer.

First, making clothes uses a huge amount of resources. Producing a single cotton T-shirt requires thousands of liters of water. When we buy clothes we rarely wear, we are wasting that water.

Second, cheap clothes do not last long. Because they are made quickly and with low-quality materials, they often lose their shape after just a few washes. As a result, many of them are thrown away and end up in landfills, where they can take many years to break down.

Some people may argue that cheap clothes help people save money. However, buying one good-quality item that lasts for years can actually cost less than buying several cheap items that wear out quickly.

Before buying new clothes, ask yourself, "Do I really need this?" Repairing old clothes, swapping with friends, or shopping at secondhand stores are great alternatives. Our choices can make a real difference for the planet.

variants.prestudy:
Clothing has never been more affordable than it is today. Many retailers sell T-shirts for roughly the price of a sandwich, and new collections appear almost every week. This phenomenon, commonly referred to as fast fashion, may appear convenient, yet I firmly believe that we ought to purchase fewer garments and wear them considerably longer.

To begin with, the production of clothing consumes an enormous quantity of resources. Manufacturing a single cotton T-shirt is estimated to require thousands of liters of water, which means that every garment we purchase but seldom wear represents water that has been needlessly wasted.

Furthermore, inexpensive clothing is rarely designed to endure. Having been manufactured hastily from low-quality materials, such garments frequently lose their shape after only a handful of washes. As a result, a substantial proportion of them are discarded and eventually accumulate in landfills, where they can take many years to decompose.

Admittedly, some people may contend that cheap clothing allows consumers to save money. Nevertheless, investing in a single durable, high-quality item that lasts for years can, in the long run, prove less expensive than repeatedly buying several cheap items that wear out quickly.

Before purchasing new clothes, therefore, we should ask ourselves, "Do I genuinely need this?" Repairing worn clothing, exchanging garments with friends, and shopping at secondhand stores are all worthwhile alternatives. Ultimately, the choices we make as consumers can make a meaningful difference for the planet.
